Between the port and the 787 campus: SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 for North Charleston NDT technicians

North Charleston fits very different inspection work into a few miles of the Cooper River and the airport. Boeing South Carolina fabricates, assembles and delivers all three 787 Dreamliner models here, and in November 2025 it broke ground on a new final assembly building and an expansion of its Interiors Responsibility Center as it works toward ten airplanes a month in 2026. Joint Base Charleston flies the C-17. Along the river, the shipyard, the container terminals and the steel and chemical plants inspect to construction and pressure codes. Which of those places you work in decides the document behind your certification. For the side-by-side detail, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Three Lowcountry technicians, three different answers

The crane and hull inspector. A Level II doing MT and UT on ship-to-shore crane welds or hull repairs at the yard on the old navy base works under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, because the AWS and ASME codes and owners' specifications behind those jobs call for it. Navy ship repair adds NAVSEA requirements on top.

The supplier inspector. A penetrant or ultrasonic technician at a company machining details, forming ducts or building interior parts for airframe programs usually meets NAS 410, or its European twin EN 4179, in a purchase-order quality clause. That clause flows down to every sub-tier shop that tests the hardware, and Nadcap AC7114 auditors check it wherever the site holds accreditation.

The airlift-wing maintainer. Airmen and civilian employees keeping C-17s flying at Joint Base Charleston work under Air Force directives and contract terms, not under a document the individual picks. After separation, the next civilian employer's Level 3 decides what those records are worth.

Inside an aircraft maker's own inspection departments, the company's written practice governs. Ask its Level 3 which standard and revision that practice names; a recruiter's summary is not a reliable answer.

Moving from the river to the airport

Most local career moves run from industrial work toward aerospace. An SNT-TC-1A certificate does not meet a NAS 410 requirement on its own. The receiving shop's Responsible Level 3 (RL3) reviews your file and decides which earlier training, experience and examinations to credit. Penetrant and magnetic particle are where people from the port and the plants most often come up short, since NAS 410 calls for more formal training in those surface methods, delivered against approved outlines with the hours recorded. Veterans of the Navy nuclear pipeline trained in Goose Creek should collect transcripts and any civilian NDT records before applying: a service qualification is evidence for the RL3 to weigh, not a civilian certification.

A record file that survives a job change

  • Course certificates showing the outline, the instructor and the hours for each method.
  • An experience log signed as you earn it, split by method and level.
  • Examination results and the certification letter from every employer.
  • A vision record that has not lapsed.

Both schemes are employer-based. When you change jobs, this evidence is the only thing that goes with you, and the new employer certifies you again under its own program.

For Tri-County suppliers running two programs

Plenty of shops in Charleston, Berkeley and Dorchester counties take aerospace and industrial orders in the same building. Keep the two certification programs clearly apart, print the governing standard and revision on each certification, and plan the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, on the dates your customers set. Nadcap and customer auditors pick a signed report and follow it back to the inspector's training, experience, examinations and eyesight records. The NAS 410 audit documentation page for North Charleston explains how Atlantis prepares and reviews those records for your RL3 to approve. Written practices for aerospace work are covered on aerospace written practice development.

What Atlantis can and cannot do in the Lowcountry

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. You study theory online at your own pace with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, rehearse in the aircraft hangar scenes of the Practical NDT simulator, and complete the hands-on work and the practical examination at your employer's site under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in North Charleston. The aerospace NDT training page for North Charleston shows how that route fits aircraft work, and our ASNT Level III consulting builds written practices on SNT-TC-1A aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114. Atlantis inspection in the US covers UT, MT, PT and VT.

For anyone weighing a move into the 787 supply chain, the position is simple: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. Ask the hiring shop's RL3 whether SNT-TC-1A-based coursework will be credited before you sign up for it. How NAS 410 programs run is set out in NAS 410 explained.
